summary: Ouachita County lookout tower of the Arkansas Forestry Commission, all steel and about 110 ft high in a 1941 survey. No current source describes the site.

facts.design: all-steel tower with an enclosed cabin at the top

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey station description calls it a lookout tower of the Arkansas Forestry Commission, about 110 feet high, already in place.

evidence.supports: described by the Coast and Geodetic Survey in 1941
evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1941 (KBJ)

evidence.supports: lookout tower of the Arkansas Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: STATION IS A LOOKOUT TOWER OF THE ARKANSAS FORESTRY COMMISSION.

evidence.supports: about 2.5 miles south of Holly Springs; all steel construction
evidence.quote: S OF HOLLY SPRINGS. STATION IS ALL STEEL CONSTRUCTION AND HAS

evidence.supports: enclosed cabin at the top; tower about 110 feet high
evidence.quote: AN ENCLOSED CABIN AT THE TOP. THE TOWER IS ABOUT 110 FEET HIGH.

evidence.supports: Arkansas Forestry Commission created by Act 234 in 1931 and built many towers
evidence.quote: The Arkansas Forestry Commission was established by Act 234 in 1931, and it too built many more towers.

evidence.supports: 122 known fire towers at the height of operation
evidence.quote: At the height of their operation, Arkansas had 122 known fire towers.

evidence.supports: 48 still stood in 1994; unknown whether any were in use
evidence.quote: In 1994, forty-eight still stood, but it is unknown if any were still in use.

notes_for_editor: The 1941 station description is a clear, dated source for design, agency and height (110 ft = 33.5 m, matching the record's height_m). It gives no build date, so the tower is only known to exist by 1941. The record's status, access, staffing and current condition are unknown; no source describes the site now. The Central US Lookouts page is the only tower-specific source; the Encyclopedia of Arkansas is general context. The 1985 USGS quad named on the station page is not used.
